newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Seoul bus drivers agree to end strike.
newsitem.headline: Seoul bus drivers agree to end strike.

text.p: Striking public bus drivers in Seoul on Wednesday agreed to go back to work after accepting a 5.5 percent wage hike, sharply lower than the 13 percent they had orginally demanded, municipal officials said.

Drivers walked out early on Wednesday along with bus workers in two other cities, Taejon and Inchon. Yonhap Television News reported that Taejon drivers had also accepted a pay settlement to end their industrial action.

The municipal officials said management had accepted the Seoul bus drivers' demand for an additional half-month bonus payment per year. They were unable to confirm the television report of the Taejon settlement.

The strikes were the first since a new labour law came into force this month. Labour experts said the quick resolution in Seoul augured well for the nation's annual wage round. South Korea was hit by a month of strikes following the passage of an earlier version of the labour law on December 26. The strikes forced President Kim Young-sam to return the bill to parliament for revision.
"Unions have used up a lot of their fighting power in their earlier industrial action," said Bae Sohn-keun, a labour expert at Korea University.
